text:
nightly-bot: Nightly perf alert: runtime-serving p95 latency +28% vs baseline (24h), throughput -12%. Spike started ~1774972000. Affected: kernel selector + prefetch paths. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/nightly/perf/1775 :eyes:

maya: Ack, seeing the alert. Checking recent merges to staging and dedicated.

david: I bisected staging window earlier — points to merge of PR #4621 (merged 1774979001) 'prefetch: expand lookahead to 32 tokens / adjust kernel fallback ordering'. Repro locally w/ perf harness.

li: Does that PR modify the kernel selection matrix? I thought it only touched prefetch heuristics.

david: It flips two flags used by kernel selector so yes, it changes fallback ordering for short vs long seq. Also increases prefetch aggressiveness which seems to interact with KV cache.

sam: I can reproduce in perf-harness with the nightly trace. Command I ran: ```bash
./perf-run --profile night-longseq --model redwood-7b --seed 42 --concurrency 40 --duration 300
```
Output snippets: ```
p50: 24ms -> 26ms
p95: 210ms -> 275ms
throughput: 190 req/s -> 168 req/s
kv_evictions/sec: 14 -> 92
batch_size_avg: 8.2 -> 6.1
```

ci-bot: Perf CI: PR 4621 triggered perf check on linux-gpu-rt-1. Result: FAIL (p95 +22% > threshold). Logs: https://ci.redwood/4621/perf.

maya: Ok, this is a rollout blocker. Two immediate options: revert PR for now or craft a targeted fix (reduce lookahead back to 16 and keep kernel order). Revert is faster. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

ryan: +1 revert for immediate mitigation. We can iterate on a safer prefetch patch with controlled canary. I suggest revert -> canary -> validate.

li: Quick profiling I ran (nvprof + kv counters) shows KV cache miss rate jumped 2.4% -> 18% under the same workload. Prefetching longer sequences is causing more unique KV keys resident transiently, thrashing the small per-GPU cache and forcing more evictions -> higher mem churn -> scheduler splits batches earlier because per-request memory peaks.

maya: That matches the batch_size drop Sam saw. Good diagnostics. David, can you open a revert PR? If already open, please link.

david: Revert created: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4621-revert (PR 4635). Title: revert(prefetch): revert aggressive lookahead from #4621. Ran a quick smoke canary on dev cluster (non-prod) and p95 returned to baseline.

sam: I'll run a full canary tonight (23:00 UTC) on dev->staging path and attach load runner. Plan: 23:00 deploy revert to canary nodes (tag: canary/prefetch-revert), warm caches, run perf harness 23:20-23:40, post results in this thread.

maya: Good. CI perf on revert PR queued (should start soon). Also add a perf unit test for KV eviction regression so PRs like this fail earlier.

ryan: Also worth adding a microbenchmark for kernel selector that exercises the fallback ordering matrix with variable seq lengths. I'll pick that up.

ci-bot: Perf run queued for PR 4635 (revert). Links: https://ci.redwood/4635/perf.

maya: Action items summary: 1) Sam run canary tonight (owner: sam). 2) CI perf + smoke on PR 4635 (owner: ci-bot / eng infra). 3) Add KV-eviction perf test (owner: maya+li). 4) Ryan to add kernel selector microbenchmark. We'll revert fully if canary + CI pass. If revert passes, schedule a controlled rework of prefetch with conservative defaults.

sam: On it. I'll post canary logs here after run. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks — moving this to high priority. If anyone finds alternate root cause data before 23:00 ping here.

david: One more note: PR 4621 also touched quantization-kernel hints — we'll include those traces in the postmortem to make sure there isn't an orthogonal regression.

li: I'll collect NVTX traces and kv counters during the canary.

nightly-bot: Noted. Will keep monitoring and will post if additional anomalies occur.
